Forward-looking corporate tax planning Ontario businesses use to lower lifetime tax — entity structuring, owner-manager compensation, and multi-year deferral strategy built on the Income Tax Act, delivered by a corporate tax planning accountant with AFFORDABLE flat-fee pricing and no surprise fees.

1

Entity Structure Optimization

Corporation versus partnership, holding companies, and reorganizations structured for tax efficiency. The structure you choose at the start determines your tax exposure for years — we design and reorganize entities so income, assets, and risk sit in the right place under the Income Tax Act.

  • We transfer appreciated business assets into a corporation on a tax-deferred basis using a section 85 rollover, electing the optimal transfer price on Form T2057 so no immediate capital gain is triggered on incorporation.
  • We separate operating risk from retained wealth by moving surplus cash and investments into a holding company, keeping the operating corporation lean and protecting accumulated profits from trade creditors in your corporate tax planning Ontario structure.
  • We purify an operating corporation ahead of a future sale, stripping non-active assets so the shares stay qualified small business corporation shares and remain eligible for the Lifetime Capital Gains Exemption.
  • We carry out section 86 and section 51 reorganizations to redesign the share capital — adding growth and freeze shares — without disposing of the underlying business or triggering tax.
  • We assess whether a partnership, joint venture, or corporation gives the better result for a specific venture, weighing flow-through losses against the deferral a corporation provides through corporate tax advisory services.
2

Tax Credit & Deduction Maximization

SR&ED claims, Investment Tax Credits, and sector-specific credits identified and structured in advance. Most credits are lost not because a business is ineligible, but because the work was never documented to qualify — we plan the claim before the spending happens, not after.

  • We structure SR&ED projects so the eligible work is documented contemporaneously through the year, supporting the Form T661 claim and the 35% refundable Investment Tax Credit rather than reconstructing evidence after the fact.
  • We plan capital expenditures to land in the fiscal year where the Accelerated Investment Incentive and full expensing rules deliver the largest first-year deduction against active business income.
  • We layer the Ontario Innovation Tax Credit and Ontario Business-Research Institute Tax Credit on top of federal SR&ED, mapping each to the correct provincial schedule for a complete corporate tax planning claim.
  • We sequence the use of Investment Tax Credit carryforwards against future tax payable, claiming them in the years they deliver the most benefit within the 20-year window.
  • We identify sector credits — digital media, apprenticeship, and clean-technology incentives — that owner-managers routinely miss, included in our cost-effective service.
3

CRA Compliance & Audit Readiness

Strategic filing schedules, documentation, and audit preparation that hold up under scrutiny. The best audit defense is built before any letter arrives — we structure your filings and records so every position is supported the day it is taken, not assembled under pressure later.

  • We calculate and document safe income on hand before any intercorporate dividend is paid, so the dividend is protected from the anti-avoidance rule in subsection 55(2) that would otherwise convert it into a capital gain.
  • We prepare and retain valuation support and director resolutions at the time of every reorganization, so a section 85 or estate freeze withstands a later CRA review with documentation already in place.
  • We maintain a defensible reasonableness file for management fees and intercompany charges between associated corporations, the exact positions CRA targets first in a corporate tax audit.
  • We align the timing of elections, filings, and supporting schedules into a single annual compliance calendar, so nothing is filed late and no position is left undocumented.
  • We keep your records to CRA's standard for the full retention period, giving you affordable audit readiness with transparent pricing and no surprise fees.
4

Owner-Manager Compensation Strategy

Salary versus dividends and family remuneration, planned around the rules that now govern both. Owner-manager pay is no longer a simple split — TOSI and reasonableness tests changed the math. We design a remuneration mix that is tax-efficient and defensible under current law.

  • We apply the Tax on Split Income (TOSI) rules to family dividends, confirming each family member meets an excluded-share or excluded-business exception before any dividend is paid, so income splitting holds rather than being taxed at the top rate.
  • We test salary against the reasonableness standard for family members actually working in the business, supporting the deduction with documented hours and market-rate pay.
  • We balance owner salary to create RRSP contribution room and CPP pensionable earnings against the deferral that retaining income in the corporation provides, tuned to your personal cash needs.
  • We pay capital dividends tax-free out of the Capital Dividend Account, filing the section 83(2) election so the non-taxable half of realized capital gains reaches you without further tax.
  • We coordinate compensation with shareholder loan balances to avoid the subsection 15(2) income inclusion, a corporate tax advisory service delivered at a flat, affordable fee.
5

Cash Flow & Tax Liability Management

Optimizing cash flow while minimizing tax and planning payments efficiently. A tax bill you saw coming is a budget line; one you did not is a cash crisis. We forecast liability and time payments so your corporation always has the cash to meet CRA without straining operations.

  • We forecast your corporate tax liability mid-year from interim results, so instalments and the final balance are funded from planned cash rather than scrambled for at the deadline.
  • We time the realization of investment gains and the payment of bonuses across fiscal years to keep taxable income — and the resulting tax bill — smooth and predictable.
  • We use a bonus accrual deductible in the current year but payable within 180 days, shifting income to the owner's lower-tax year while preserving the corporate deduction.
  • We schedule dividend payments to trigger the RDTOH refund in the same year tax is otherwise payable, releasing trapped refundable tax to improve cash flow.
  • We model the after-tax cash result of each major payment decision before it is made, giving you affordable, practical corporate tax planning Ontario owners can act on.
6

Year-End & Multi-Year Strategy

Deferrals, timing tactics, and future-proof planning across more than one year. The largest savings come from decisions made across multiple years, not a single return. We plan two and three years ahead so income, deductions, and exemptions land where they are taxed least.

  • We select the optimal fiscal year-end at incorporation and on reorganization, using the resulting deferral period to push the first tax payment as far forward as the rules allow.
  • We implement an estate freeze that locks today's share value to the current owner and shifts future growth to the next generation, capping the eventual capital gain on a succession.
  • We multiply access to the Lifetime Capital Gains Exemption across family shareholders through a family trust, planning the structure years before any sale of the business.
  • We sequence non-capital loss and Investment Tax Credit carryforwards across multiple years so each is claimed before it expires and against the highest-taxed income.
  • We build a multi-year plan that anticipates rate changes and exemption limits, future-proofing your structure with transparent pricing and no hourly billing.

10 Smart Corporate Tax Planning Strategies That Save You Money

Optimize Salary-Dividend Mix

Your corporate tax planning must balance salary versus dividends based on your corporation's taxable income and personal marginal rate. Salaries create RRSP room and are deductible to the corporation; dividends avoid CPP premiums. The wrong split can cost your family thousands every year in combined tax.

Claim the Full Small Business Deduction

Strategic corporate tax planning ensures your CCPC claims the entire $500,000 business limit at the reduced federal rate under ITA section 125. If passive investment income exceeds $50,000, the SBD gets clawed back dollar for dollar. We monitor this threshold quarterly so you never lose the deduction unexpectedly.

Use a Holding Company Structure

Transferring excess retained earnings to a holding corporation through tax-free intercorporate dividends under ITA subsection 112(1) is core corporate tax planning. This protects surplus cash from operating risk, enables estate freeze strategies, and defers personal tax until shareholders actually withdraw funds.

Accelerate or Defer Expenses

Timing major purchases around your fiscal year-end is a practical corporate tax planning move. Prepaying rent, bonuses declared within 179 days, or purchasing equipment before year-end to trigger Accelerated CCA on Schedule 8 can reduce your current-year corporate tax bill significantly without changing your actual spending.

Maximize SR&ED Tax Credits

If your corporation performs any experimental development or technological improvement, file a T661 claim for the Scientific Research and Experimental Development credit. Eligible CCPCs recover up to 35% of qualified SR&ED expenditures as a refundable credit. Missing this in your corporate tax planning leaves serious money unclaimed.

Plan CRA Instalment Payments

CRA charges compound interest on late or insufficient corporate tax instalments. Proper tax planning calculates whether the prior-year, second prior-year, or current-year method produces the lowest quarterly payment. Choosing the wrong instalment base ties up cash your corporation could deploy elsewhere.

Utilize the Capital Dividend Account

Every corporate tax plan should track your CDA balance after capital gains, life insurance proceeds, and eligible capital property dispositions. Filing Form T2054 lets you distribute these amounts completely tax-free to shareholders. Ignoring this account means your shareholders pay personal tax they never owed.

Split Income With Family Members

Corporate tax planning includes paying reasonable salaries to family members who perform genuine work in the business. This shifts income to lower-bracket individuals, reduces combined family tax, and survives TOSI rules under ITA section 120.4 when the recipient is over 24 and actively involved.

Time Your Bonus Accrual

Declare a management bonus before your corporation's fiscal year-end and pay it within 179 days to deduct it in the current year while deferring personal tax to the next calendar year. This corporate tax planning tactic legally shifts income across two tax years, smoothing both corporate and personal obligations.

Review Your Tax Plan Annually

Tax legislation changes every federal budget. Annual corporate tax planning reviews catch new credits, rate changes, and compliance risks before your T2 is due. Corporations that skip this step routinely overpay tax or face CRA penalties from outdated structures that no longer meet current rules.
